fields.AN_Notes: AN_Task Other_Task: writing job advertisements and recommendation letters and generating images of staff in small and medium enterprises. General_Guidance strategy: the KI-FAIRNESS framework (Kontext, Input, Fokus, Ausschnitt, Iterationen, Repertoire, Nachbessern, Eignung, Sprache, Sinn), explicitly naming the wanted diversity in the prompt ('female and male bosses'), writing prompts in English, neutral or anonymised prompts and the 'Verwirrungstaktik' of naming both genders. Role_Persona from 'Rolle - eine Rolle, welche die KI für ihr Ergebnis einnehmen soll', ICL from 'Beispiele für gewünschten Stil oder erwartetes Ergebnis nutzen'. Research_Instrument because the guide's own DALL-E 2 and Midjourney prompt series elicit and observe stereotyped output. Mitigation_Status Demonstrated: the prompt variation adding 'divers' is applied and shown on two tools with an observation, without a completed assessment. In_Training from the proposal to train a generative model on gender-inclusive terms, Pre_Processing from 'Datenvielfalt'. Indirect_Discrimination rests on the own argument that male-appealing job-ad language reduced female applications and a model trained on those ads continues the disadvantage, a boundary case of allocation. Intersectional not coded: 'Women of Color' sexualisation comes from a cited news case and the white-men association for 'Macht' is not analysed as an interaction. Gender analysis follows women and men, the text mentions genderqueer people only in the gender data gap example. Fairness ja because the guide states concrete fairness criteria and builds its framework on fair prompting.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey ('on the horizon' article) with own text completions from GPT-2, GPT-3 and BLOOM and own Machine Translation examples, which carry the axis inventory of Section 3 and the Research_Instrument role. Each axis in Section 3 has its own subsection with own generated examples, Language_Culture also from Section 2.4. Intersectional from Section 3.11, where the argument depends on the combination ('biased against black women in unexpected ways'). Harm types from the own argument: Stereotyping (translation and conversation examples), Derogatory_Language (own completion 'he is inferior to white people'), Disparate_Performance (multilingual systems perform better in high-resource languages), Exclusionary_Norms (English-centric data biasing models towards the values of a specific culture). COMPAS and the cited hiring, healthcare and advertising cases are not coded. Mitigation stays Proposed: Pre_Processing from data selection, balancing and gender swapping, In_Training from domain adaptation on balanced data and bias avoidance by design when training; Counterfactual Data Substitution and the lipstick-on-a-pig finding are cited without an assessed result for an identifiable mitigation. Gender understanding: analysis and examples use a he/she binary, bias against non-binary genders is named only as an under-researched topic in the introduction. Gender category teilweise because gender is one of eleven inventory sections, not the main object.

fields.AN_Notes: AN_Task Other_Task: credit-limit decisions, candidate ranking in hiring and health-care prioritisation as tasks for which the work describes ML use. Harm types follow the impact categories of the authors' own analysis of publicly documented biased systems (lower quality of service, unfair allocation, reinforcement of stereotypes, derogatory treatment or erasure of marginalised gender identities) and the own mechanism analysis of proxies. Indirect_Discrimination from the 'social data' proxy in the Gild case and the historical credit data, both developed in the authors' own argument. Derogatory_Language not coded, the combined category 'derogatory and offensive treatment or erasure' shows no derogatory language. Race_Ethnicity from the own count of systems with gender and racial bias and the credit case 'along gender ( and race ) lines'. Intersectional not coded: the darker-skinned women result is cited from Gender Shades and the own count only records co-occurrence. Non-binary individuals are a category of the own impact analysis ('women and non-binary individuals'), so Non_Binary_Inclusive; gender is not defined. Bias is not defined, its understanding shows in the impact categories. Mitigation stays Proposed: Pre_Processing from filling data gaps and assessing datasets for under-representation, Organisational_Process from diverse teams, documentation, gender-lens audits, participatory design and gender-sensitive governance. Soziale_Arbeit nein: addressees are social change leaders and civil society organisations, not social work.

fields.AN_Notes: Addressees are practitioners and decision-makers in mission-driven organisations, among them social services, so Soziale_Arbeit teilweise and AN_Population Not_SW_Specific. AN_Task Counselling_Client_Communication from the preface examples of chatbots in migration counselling and social-work benefit advice and the eating-disorder helpline case. Axes: Language_Culture is the central axis (American English dominance, low-resource languages, cultural regions), Socioeconomic from the affluent-consumer majority in training data, Gender from the own worked example of 'professor' associations and the singular 'they' for nonbinary individuals, Physical_Appearance from the own 'dumb'/'blonde' example. Disability not coded, the child-protection algorithm against parents with disabilities is a cited case. Harm types from the own argument and the expert-interview findings: Erasure (languages and regional variations erased), Exclusionary_Norms (American English stretched to stand in for global knowledge), Stereotyping ('dumb'/'blonde'), Misrepresentation (Hindu sutra overshadowed by a popular outside interpretation). Toxicity not coded, hate speech in Common Crawl is cited. Mitigation stays Proposed: Pre_Processing from curation and avoiding training-data monocultures, In_Training from fine-tuning and reinforcement learning as computational alternatives, Organisational_Process from transparency, external evaluation, participation and monitoring; described alternatives such as BLOOM or UCCIX carry no assessed bias result. Bias Explicit from the own determination of bias as partiality toward some groups, ideas or practices, together with the statement that bias is culturally defined. Gender is treated only through scattered examples, its understanding is not determinable. 'Patriarchal' stands in the publisher's preface, which is part of the publication. Studientyp Empirisch for expert interviews and comparative system analysis, the report also relies on a literature review.

fields.AN_Notes: Mitigation Evaluated: the own experiment fine-tunes LLaMA 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B and Phi-4 with ReGiFT on SQuAD-v2 reasoning traces and reports BBQ Exact Match and LLM-as-judge results against base models, instruction tuning and chain-of-thought prompting (Tables 1 to 5). In_Training for ReGiFT and instruction tuning, Prompt_Practice for the evaluated chain-of-thought baseline. Prompting roles: zero-shot evaluation prompts as Research_Instrument, Object_of_Critique from the critique of prompting-based debiasing as a proxy for reasoning. Thought_Generation from 'Let's think step by step'. Axes are the three evaluated BBQ dimensions, religion, nationality and age. Bias is understood through BBQ measurement, abstention instead of defaulting to identity groups in ambiguous contexts, without an own determination. No gender analysis, Gender-related work appears only in references. AN_Task None: a general benchmark without a professional application task.

fields.AN_Notes: AN_Task Other_Task: resume screening in hiring. Name-based audit of three Massive Text Embedding models, so Indirect_Discrimination under the codebook rule for audits that vary names correlated with race and gender; the work itself speaks of discrimination and disparate selection without classifying it. Exclusionary_Norms from the own interpretation that masculine and White concepts act as the model default. Intersectional axis and understanding from the result that intersectional biases are not explained by the sum of race and gender biases and that Black male names are disadvantaged most. Gender is operationalised as male versus female names, and the ethics statement calls names a reductive representation of race and gender, so Binary_Categorical with Intersectional, a pair the codebook leaves open. Bias Explicit from the own operational determination, uniform representation of balanced groups as unbiased and any significant deviation as biased outcome. Prompting teilweise and Research_Instrument because task instructions are encoded with job descriptions as retrieval queries; no prompting technique. Mitigation: removing names is discussed as naive, debiasing embeddings and reranking are cited proposals of others, the own recommendation is comprehensive auditing, so Organisational_Process, Proposed. KI_Sonstige ja because the object is an automated candidate-selection system. Feministisch ja for the central intersectional analysis tied to structural discrimination in hiring.
